slides.label: WHO YOU BECOME
slides.sub: In Guardian, your character grows with every clean day.

posts.caption:
Nobody becomes free overnight. You grow into it.

In Guardian, you pick a journey (the mage, the warrior, the ranger, the astronaut or the explorer) and your character grows with every day you stay clean. From an apprentice with a candle to someone who doesn't need it anymore.

The first days are the hardest. They're also the ones that count the most.

Which journey would you choose? 👇

posts.name: halt
posts.caption:
Next time an urge shows up, ask yourself four questions: Am I hungry? Angry? Lonely? Tired?

It's called HALT, and it's used in recovery programs for a reason. Very often the urge isn't about what it seems to be about. It's your body asking for food, rest, connection or a way to let off steam.

Eat something. Call someone. Go to bed. Then see if the urge is still there. 🍃

posts.name: breathe-with-him
posts.caption:
When the urge comes, don't fight it. Breathe through it.

In for 4. Hold for 7. Out for 8. One slow round is often enough to break the autopilot and let the wave pass.

Save this for the next hard moment. 🫁

posts.name: the-astronaut

slides.label: THE ASTRONAUT
slides.lead: Lost the signal for a while?
slides.sub: Every slip is a course correction, not the end of the mission.

posts.caption:
Every astronaut loses the signal sometimes. What matters is what you do next.

A slip doesn't erase the distance you've traveled. Check your instruments: what happened, when, how you were feeling. Then correct your course and keep going.

The mission isn't over. 🚀

posts.name: move

slides.label: URGE HACK
slides.lead: Stand up. Move for ten minutes.

posts.caption:
The simplest trick is also one of the strongest: move.

In a review of 12 studies on smokers, a single short session of exercise reduced cravings in every one of them. Porn cravings run on the same reward system, so the same move is worth trying. You don't need a gym. A brisk walk, some push-ups or a few flights of stairs will do.

Get up, get out of the room, and let your body reset. 🏃

(Source: Taylor, Ussher & Faulkner, Addiction, 2007)

posts.name: day-seven
posts.caption:
Seven days. Seven times you chose yourself, even when it would've been easier not to.

If you're hitting a week today, take a moment to be proud. If you're not there yet, this is what's waiting for you.

Drop a 💛 if you're on your way.

posts.name: kindness

slides.label: SUNDAY RESET
slides.sub: Be as gentle with yourself as you'd be with a friend.

posts.caption:
Here's the trap: you slip, you feel ashamed, and the shame makes you want to escape... right back into the habit.

The way out isn't being harder on yourself. It's being honest and kind. What happened? What was going on before? What will you do differently next time?

Talk to yourself the way you'd talk to a friend who's trying. 🧡
